nodes.summary: The ancestral paths from `i`: the lists `[i = v₀, v₁, …, v_k]` with each `v_{t+1}` a parent of `v_t` (`k ≥ 0`; the path `[i]` has no edge).
nodes.title: Ancestral paths from an individual

nodes.summary: A gene-dropping outcome: `ω i k` is the Mendelian coin of the copy `(i, k)` (`k = 0` the paternal copy, `k = 1` the maternal copy), saying which copy (`0` or `1`) of the parent `g k` of `i` it inherits. Under gene dropping all `4 ^ n` outcomes are equally likely.
nodes.title: Gene-dropping outcome

nodes.summary: A path from `i` ending at `i` is `[i]`.
nodes.title: An ancestral path returning to its start is trivial

nodes.summary: Every ancestral path from `i` starts with `i`.
nodes.title: Ancestral path as its start followed by a tail

nodes.summary: Gene-dropping kinship is symmetric.
nodes.title: Symmetry of gene-dropping kinship

nodes.summary: The kinship coefficient computed by Malécot's recursion is the probability of identity by descent under gene dropping.
nodes.title: Malécot's recursion computes gene-dropping kinship

nodes.summary: A founder `j ≠ i` that is not an ancestor of `i` has kinship `0` with `i`.
nodes.title: Zero kinship with an unrelated founder

nodes.summary: Malécot's recursion under gene dropping: if `j ≠ i` is not an ancestor of `i` and has parents `f, m`, then `φ i j = (φ i f + φ i m) / 2`.
nodes.title: Malécot's recursion

nodes.summary: `φ i i = (1 + F i) / 2` under gene dropping.
nodes.title: Self-kinship under gene dropping

nodes.summary: The kinship (coancestry) coefficient under gene dropping: the probability that a copy drawn at random from `i` and a copy drawn at random from `j` are identical by descent.
nodes.title: Kinship coefficient under gene dropping

nodes.summary: Every path in `ancPaths i` starts at `i` and is nonempty.
nodes.title: Ancestral paths are nonempty with the starting individual as head

nodes.summary: Identity by descent is symmetric.
nodes.title: Symmetry of identity by descent

nodes.summary: One step of Malécot's recursion for identity by descent.
nodes.title: Malécot's recursion step for identity by descent

nodes.summary: Two copies are identical by descent of themselves with probability `1`.
nodes.title: A gene copy is identical by descent with itself

nodes.summary: The probability, under gene dropping (independent fair Mendelian coins), that the gene copies `c` and `d` are identical by descent, i.e. descend from the same founder copy.
nodes.title: Probability of identity by descent under gene dropping

nodes.summary: The inbreeding coefficient computed by Malécot's recursion is the probability of identity by descent of the two copies of `i` under gene dropping.
nodes.title: Malécot's recursion computes the inbreeding coefficient

nodes.summary: Wright's path formula for the inbreeding coefficient (Wright 1922): if `i` has parents `f = g 0` and `m = g 1`, then `F_i = Σ (1/2) ^ (n₁ + n₂ + 1) (1 + F_A)` over common ancestors `A` of `f` and `m` (including `f` or `m` themselves) and pairs of ancestral paths from `f` and `m` to `A` (with `n₁` and `n₂` edges) that share only `A`. Here `F` is the gene-dropping inbreeding coefficient.
nodes.title: Wright's path formula

nodes.summary: The inbreeding coefficient of a founder is `0`.
nodes.title: Founders are not inbred

nodes.summary: The inbreeding coefficient of `i` is the kinship of its parents, `F i = φ f m`, under gene dropping.
nodes.title: Malécot

nodes.summary: The inbreeding coefficient under gene dropping: the probability that the two copies of `i` are identical by descent.
nodes.title: Inbreeding coefficient under gene dropping

nodes.summary: A parent is an ancestor.
nodes.title: Parents are ancestors

nodes.summary: `a` is an ancestor of `b` (a parent, a parent of a parent, …).
nodes.title: Ancestor relation in a pedigree

nodes.summary: `a` is a parent of `b`.
nodes.title: Parent relation in a pedigree

nodes.summary: The tabular kinship is symmetric.
nodes.title: Symmetry of tabular kinship

nodes.summary: Wright's path formula in kinship form: `φ i j` is the sum, over common ancestors `A` (including `i` or `j` themselves) and pairs of ancestral paths `p` from `i` to `A` and `p'` from `j` to `A` that share no individual other than `A`, of `(1/2) ^ (n₁ + n₂ + 1) * (1 + F A)`, where `n₁ + n₂ + 1 = p.length + p'.length - 1` is the number of individuals on the loop.
nodes.title: Wright's path formula

nodes.summary: The inbreeding coefficient by Malécot's recursion: `F i = φ f m` for the parents `f, m` of `i`, and `F i = 0` for a founder.
nodes.title: Inbreeding coefficient by Malécot's recursion

nodes.summary: The tabular recursion for `j < i` with `i` a founder.
nodes.title: Tabular kinship when the first individual is a later founder

nodes.summary: The tabular recursion for `j < i` with `i` a non-founder.
nodes.title: Tabular kinship when the first individual is a later non-founder

nodes.summary: The tabular recursion for `i < j` with `j` a founder.
nodes.title: Tabular kinship when the second individual is a later founder

nodes.summary: The tabular recursion for `i < j` with `j` a non-founder.
nodes.title: Tabular kinship when the second individual is a later non-founder

nodes.summary: The tabular recursion on the diagonal for a founder: `φ i i = 1 / 2`.
nodes.title: Tabular self-kinship of a founder

nodes.summary: The tabular recursion on the diagonal for a non-founder: `φ i i = (1 + φ f m) / 2`.
nodes.title: Tabular self-kinship of a non-founder

nodes.summary: The kinship coefficient by Malécot's recursion, computed in the order of the numbering (the tabular method): for `i < j`, `φ i j = (φ i f + φ i m) / 2` with `f, m` the parents of `j` and `φ i j = 0` if `j` is a founder; `φ i i = (1 + φ f m) / 2` with `f, m` the parents of `i` and `φ i i = 1 / 2` for a founder; symmetric for `j < i`.
nodes.title: Kinship coefficient by Malécot's recursion

nodes.summary: Every individual on an ancestral path from `i` is `i` or precedes it.
nodes.title: Individuals on an ancestral path are its start or precede it

nodes.summary: Ancestors precede their descendants.

nodes.summary: The only ancestral path from a founder is `[i]`.

nodes.title: Ancestral paths from a non-founder

nodes.summary: No individual is the offspring of a selfing (father ≠ mother), as in Wright's setting of a bisexual population.

nodes.summary: A copy of a non-founder descends from the chosen copy of the corresponding parent.

nodes.summary: The founder copy from which the gene copy `c = (i, k)` descends under the gene-dropping outcome `ω`: a founder copy is its own origin; a copy of a non-founder descends from the copy `ω i k` of its parent `g k`.
nodes.title: Founder origin of a gene copy

nodes.summary: The ancestral paths from `i` that end at `A`.
nodes.title: Ancestral paths ending at a given ancestor

nodes.summary: A pedigree on the individuals `Fin n`, numbered so that parents precede their children (every finite pedigree, a finite DAG, has such a numbering). `parents i = some g` means that `g 0` is the father and `g 1` the mother of `i`; `parents i = none` means that `i` is a founder. Founders are unrelated and not inbred (their `2 n_F` gene copies are distinct).
nodes.title: Pedigree

nodes.summary: `[i]` is an ancestral path from `i`.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
